data.gender_notes: Alie is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word αλειπω (aleipo), meaning 'to wipe away, soothe, or console'. In ancient Greece, this name was associated with the goddesses Hygieia and Aphrodite, who offered healing, compassion, and love. In Christianity, Alie may symbolize the comforting presence of the Holy Spirit. The name Alie carries the meaning “Gentle, noble, otherworldly” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Alie usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle, noble, otherworldly and live with faith, good character and purpose.
